subject: Security exhibit: pen-test window, staging access, and evidence cadence (Vantage Health)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@vantagehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Vantage Health Legal <legal@vantagehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft security exhibit + proposed pen-test window

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our draft Security Exhibit / addendum (Vantage_Security_Addendum_v1.pdf) with two items we want to confirm before we sign the order form:

1) Pen-test window: we are proposing an initial two-week window in October (10/06 - 10/19) and would like only one scheduled window per contract year. Please confirm whether Redwood can commit to that cadence or if you require more frequent windows.

2) Staging/access: our ops team prefers the pen test run against a staging replica with sanitized data. We can provide a jumpbox and time-limited SSH keys but need confirmation on what evidence/logs Redwood will make available (raw request traces, tokenized logs, audit trail) and how long those artifacts are retained.

Also attaching a short spreadsheet that lists data types we consider out-of-scope for inspections.

Can you and legal take a look and flag any redlines? If possible, propose language for the Notice period (we proposed 72 hours) and any carveouts for PII.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this week to speed alignment.

--
Daniel Park
Senior Security Manager, Vantage Health
daniel.park@vantagehealth.com
Attachment: Vantage_Security_Addendum_v1.pdf (PDF, 245KB), Vantage_Data_Scope.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit + proposed pen-test window

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear draft. Quick responses and suggested edits below:

- Pen-test cadence: Redwood's standard is one formal inspection window per 12 months with an option for an emergency/forensic window under a separate engagement. We can commit to the single annual window you requested; we suggest a two-week window is sufficient.

- Notice period: 72 hours is workable for a scheduled window. For emergency forensic work we require 48–72 hours depending on scope; will add that differentiation into the exhibit text.

- Staging & evidence: we can support running tests against your sanitized staging environment. Operationally we need:
  * temporary access via a jumpbox with time-limited keys (recommended TTL = 8 hours per tester session)
  * a brief runbook describing the network egress rules for the staging replica
  * list of evidence packages Redwood will share after completion — our standard is: redwood-ctx.log (request traces, redacted tokens), infra-audit.log (access timeline), and an executive summary with remediation notes. Retention: default 90 days post-engagement unless you request longer.

I've attached our pen-test guidance doc (redwood-pen-test-guidance.pdf) with suggested exhibit language and a sample clause that narrows inspection to non-production PII.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute sync Wednesday (Aug 13) to align legal language and confirm the calendar? I dropped an ICS for a tentative slot.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-pen-test-guidance.pdf (PDF, 130KB), PenTest_Window_Calendar.ics (ICS)

Hi Jonas / Daniel —

We reviewed the draft and have three proposed clarifications to the exhibit itself:

1) Scope carveouts: Vantage requests that the exhibit explicitly exclude any inspection of production PII and live patient records; the exhibit should be limited to sanitized staging artifacts. We added a tab in the attached spreadsheet (Vantage_Data_Scope.xlsx) with data categories (PHI, raw clinical images, live message queues) that must remain out-of-scope.

2) Access notice: we prefer a 48-hour minimum notice for scheduled windows and a 5-business-day notice for any testing that involves simulated traffic generation.

3) Evidence samples: please provide a short list of sample artifact types you will deliver post-test (e.g., request trace with redaction placeholders, infra access timeline, remediation plan). Also confirm retention policy and whether artifacts will be stored in the customer's GCP bucket or Redwood's secure bucket.

If Redwood can update the exhibit language to reflect the carveouts and confirm retention/hosting, we can expedite internal signoff.

Regards,

Cameron Liu (on behalf of Vantage Health Legal)
Counsel, Vantage Health
legal@vantagehealth.com
Attachment: Vantage_Data_Scope.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@vantagehealth.com>, Vantage Health Legal <legal@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit + proposed pen-test window

Cameron / Daniel —

Thanks for the quick review. Summary of agreed updates and action items (so legal and ops are aligned):

- Scope: Redwood will explicitly exclude production PII / live clinical records from any inspection in the exhibit and confirm that the test target is a sanitized staging replica.

- Notice: we'll update the exhibit to state 48 hours notice for standard scheduled windows, and 5 business days for any traffic-generation or load-oriented testing. Emergency/forensic windows will be handled via a separate statement of work.

- Evidence: Redwood will deliver the following within 7 business days of completion:
  * request-trace-redacted.log (redactions indicated with <<REDACTED>> placeholders)
  * infra-access-timeline.csv (timestamped account/role access events)
  * executive-remediation-summary.pdf (high-level findings and suggested mitigations)
Retention: evidence will be stored in a customer-designated GCP bucket for 90 days by default. If Vantage requests extended retention, we will include it as an opt-in appendix and provide estimated costs.

- Staging access: the jumpbox approach with time-limited keys is fine. Recommended tester session TTL = 8 hours; Redwood will provide a runbook template that lists the egress rules and observed interfaces.

Action items / owners: 
  * Redwood (Jonas) -> update exhibit language and return a redline by EOD Thu Aug 14.
  * Vantage (Cameron) -> confirm whether the 48-hour vs 72-hour notice compromise is acceptable for standard windows (reply by Thu Aug 14).
  * Karthik (cc) -> please prepare a short ops appendix with the evidence file naming conventions and a sample retention policy note.

I've created a Jira for tracking: SEC-342 and shared a Drive folder with the draft exhibit (link below). I also tentatively scheduled a 30-min sync for Aug 14 at 11:00; please confirm or propose another time.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-342, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBvEXAMPLElink

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
